title: Months of AI-assisted game development. Definitely more than just a prompt – my little side project PAN!CiTY.
author: chick0rn
selftext:
I thought I'd share a little update on my side project, PAN!CiTY, a physics-based city builder with a rather chaotic approach to urban planning.

I've been using AI throughout development, but I really wanted to create something with its own identity rather than just generate a game and call it a day.

There is no one-shot-prompt behind this project. It's a constantly evolving collection of ideas, rules and gameplay mechanics. I spend a lot of time figuring out how these systems should interact, playtesting them, balancing things and making manual adjustments. Sometimes an idea sounds great on paper but just doesn't work when you actually play it.

The visual side has been a similar process. I originally built the first buildings myself using Asset Forge by Kenney.nl. With the help of AI, I gradually refined and expanded those assets until I had a consistent visual foundation that I could use to generate the remaining buildings.

For development, I've used both Sol and Opus and am currently working with Gemini Neon.

My goal was never to see how quickly I could generate a game. I wanted to make a game that I would actually enjoy playing myself.

I'm not interested in producing AI slop or pumping out generic games. PAN!CiTY is a personal creative project that I genuinely enjoy spending my free time on. AI allows me to tackle a project of this scale, but there's still a lot of manual work, creative decisions and trial and error involved.

There's plenty of work left, but I wanted to share where the project currently stands.
